result.report:
PASS for the exact finite two-graph classification in the declared real scalar extension. The argument establishes the criterion for each prescribed positive-growth reference and every bounded continuous real-PA obstacle on finite rational spatial domains, including nonseparable data. The original arbitrary-balanced-space P05.2 remains open.

The intersection algebra checks out independently. Primitive quotient normals use saturated face lattices; the cone indices in (6) are correct. Summing the first-divisor weights proves balancing, and (M) proves mixed commutativity with real coefficients. Refinement compatibility applies successively after first-divisor balancing is established. Consequently new refinement vertices inherit zero second weight unless they inherit an existing atom. The degree identity follows by cancellation on bounded edges and zero slopes of the bounded difference on unbounded edges. No factorial division occurs.

The finite-cone construction (FC1)–(FC4) correctly characterizes continuous PA actual-PC functions. Necessity uses rational endpoints and small rational steps. Sufficiency establishes convexity along contained segments, then groups initial tangent directions to handle remote endpoints on every permitted structure and every real centre. Tangential slots, zero displacements and lineality are retained. The resulting rational cone justifies the exact positive-growth decomposition (FC6): the rational box lies in the reference's active face and preserves every strict recession inequality. This supplies rational localizations whose positive sum equals the original real reference, without introducing irrational spatial comparison walls.

Graph convexity tests the entire relation cone K_v, rather than merely the actual weight vector. Product projection (G2) is valid because grouped projected tangent vectors remain in the factor tangent cones and sum to zero. The PC-to-PAPC argument also checks every required ordinary-open local cycle: rational balanced incident generators give Jensen tests, and linearity extends positivity to all real incident weights. Both positive cycle dimensions on this carrier are covered.

The positive cylinder proof establishes the full product envelope. Partial infima preserve rational graph PCC inequalities; finiteness propagates through vertices, bounded edges, cycles and ends. The scalar completion has finite outgoing derivatives. The incidence system is feasible using γ−||u||∞, and coordinatewise maxima yield its greatest feasible assignment. Fourier elimination has rational variable coefficients because connected rank-one graphs have rational weight ratios. Touching supports of rational vertical slices then dominate every raw competitor at rational product points. Rational enclosing same-face PCCs extend this domination to all real centres without assuming raw continuity. Together with (19), this proves global raw equality and two-sided growth.

The rational-domain step is substantive and valid. Although dual chamber endpoints may be real, the supergradient endpoints and normal generators in (21)–(22) are rational. Their maximization domains form a finite rational complex, with vertices only over graph nodes. Thus the construction does not rely on joint convexity of bilinear interpolation or on rational walls inferred from real coefficients.

Complete contact follows at every possible atom. A singleton exposed interval gives zero second divisor. For a nondegenerate exposed interval at a noncontact point, coercivity forces a strict obstacle cap; greatest-assignment maximality forces the vertex Laplacian to vanish. Positive weights then force each outgoing slope function to be affine. The rank-one kernel condition produces (27), whose residual first divisor is supported on a rational hyperplane where the residual function vanishes. Its complete second divisor is therefore zero. This includes junction fibres, inserted edge fibres, rectangle interiors and ends. Finite components and their actual positive product scalars are correctly restored.

The higher-rank obstruction is also complete. An extreme nonnegative relation has proper support; otherwise a two-sided kernel perturbation contradicts extremality. Hence M>0. The cap (HR3) satisfies all intrinsic graph-PC inequalities and glues continuously through upward edge bends. Product convexity follows from the verified projection lemma. Exact rational-reference localization and positive summation give an actual-PC, actual-PAPC potential equal to the prescribed reference outside a compact set. Supported PCCs first pin rational fibre centres, then edge interpolation and rational enclosing PCCs pin every real centre throughout the bump. Outside the bump the ceiling directly gives the bound, proving HR16 under the stated raw class.

The higher-rank primitive-normal calculation retains both intermediate contributions: graph axes contribute 2klMw_H and transverse axes contribute 2klMw_H, where k=δε and l=δb. The complete coefficient is therefore 4δ²εbMw_H. In the rank-one two-branch construction, the kink indices Q/g and P/g are retained; the two axis families contribute 4ab each, giving 8ab before scaling by κ². The gaps vanish at every other original measure vertex, and obstacle refinements introduce only zero-weight atoms. Thus the complete integrals are exactly −4δ²εbMw_H and −8κ²ab, respectively.

For every constructed envelope, P+1/n is an explicit uniform decreasing PAPC regularization in γ+O(1), with identical finite measures. The failure cases exhaust the complement of the criterion because strict positive balancing makes every local relation cone have rank at least one.

I authenticated the definition identifiers, recursive normalization and quoted proof boundaries against the [BMPS v1 primary PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1). The supplied mathematical dependency chain is self-contained; the general source theorem proofs and existing one-dimensional dossier are comparison material, not essential premises. Harmless corrections: distinguish the coercivity constant B from the selected graph vertex B; interpret the refinement cancellation as concerning the two inherited pieces, with additional incident pieces carrying zero inherited weight; and render the flattened multiplier Sε in the comparison extract of Lemma 3.4 as S/ε. These require no substantive change to the main argument.
